headline_marked: India win by 40 runs, [[Bangladesh women's team out of Asia Cup]]
headline: India win by 40 runs, Bangladesh women's team out of Asia Cup
summary: India posted 149/6, while Bangladesh managed only 109/7, ending their campaign in the first semi-final.
details: Bangladesh women's team has been eliminated from the Asia Cup after losing to India by 40 runs in the first semi-final held in Dubai.
After winning the toss and inviting India to bat first, Bangladesh's bowling attack struggled to contain the team from India, who scored 149 runs for the loss of 6 wickets.
India's Shafali Verma led the scoring with a half-century, finishing with 64 runs, while captain Harmanpreet Kaur remained unbeaten on 24 runs.
In response, Bangladesh struggled to build any significant partnerships. Despite a 26-run opening stand, the batting line-up failed to reach the target.
Swarna Akter remained unbeaten on 22 runs, the highest individual score for Bangladesh, while Dilara Akter scored 21 runs.
The Bangladesh women's team finished their innings at 109 runs for the loss of 7 wickets, falling short of the victory target.
caption:
A tough exit for the Tigresses. Bangladesh women's team crashes out of the Asia Cup after a 40-run defeat to India.

Bangladesh women's team has been eliminated from the Asia Cup after losing to India by 40 runs in the first semi-final held in Dubai.

After winning the toss and inviting India to bat first, Bangladesh's bowling attack struggled to contain the team from India, who scored 149 runs for the loss of 6 wickets.

India's Shafali Verma led the scoring with a half-century, finishing with 64 runs, while captain Harmanpreet Kaur remained unbeaten on 24 runs.

In response, Bangladesh struggled to build any significant partnerships. Despite a 26-run opening stand, the batting line-up failed to reach the target.

Swarna Akter remained unbeaten on 22 runs, the highest individual score for Bangladesh, while Dilara Akter scored 21 runs.

The Bangladesh women's team finished their innings at 109 runs for the loss of 7 wickets, falling short of the victory target.

topic: pm urges students to show love for animals
headline_marked: PM Tareq Rahman [[urges students to care for animals]] and nature
headline: PM Tareq Rahman urges students to care for animals and nature
summary: The Prime Minister met with students from various schools and colleges, emphasizing the importance of environmental protection and holistic development.
details: Prime Minister Tareq Rahman called upon students to show love and care for all animals and protect nature and the environment on Thursday.
During a meeting at the National Parliament House, he stated that as the best of all creations, it is the responsibility of humans to take care of plants and animals without harming them.
The Prime Minister encouraged students to plant more trees, keep their surroundings clean, and develop a responsible attitude toward nature and animals from a young age.
He also urged students to engage in regular sports and cultural activities, including music, poetry recitation, drawing, and playing musical instruments, alongside their studies.
Highlighting the physical and mental benefits of sports, he noted that regular exercise helps maintain health and while fostering discipline, self-confidence, and teamwork.
The meeting included students and teachers from Puthia Girls' High School, Savar High Girls' School, Tejgaon Women's College, and Shafiuddin Sarkar Academy and College.
The students, who also witnessed a session of the National Parliament, expressed their excitement and inspiration from the Prime Minister's guidance.
caption:
Care for animals and nature: PM Tareq Rahman shares a vision for a greener, more compassionate future with students.

Prime Minister Tareq Rahman called upon students to show love and care for all animals and protect nature and the environment on Thursday.

During a meeting at the National Parliament House, he stated that as the best of all creations, it is the responsibility of humans to take care of plants and animals without harming them.

The Prime Minister encouraged students to plant more trees, keep their surroundings clean, and develop a responsible attitude toward nature and animals from a young age.

He also urged students to engage in regular sports and cultural activities, including music, poetry recitation, drawing, and playing musical instruments, alongside their studies.

Highlighting the physical and mental benefits of sports, he noted that regular exercise helps maintain health and while fostering discipline, self-confidence, and teamwork.

The meeting included students and teachers from Puthia Girls' High School, Savar High Girls' School, Tejgaon Women's College, and Shafiuddin Sarkar Academy and College.

The students, who also witnessed a session of the National Parliament, expressed their excitement and inspiration from the Prime Minister's guidance.
